§6Rocket Engines§f are the thrust source for every AR rocket. The basic Monopropellant Rocket Engine burns monopropellant fuel for short-range and atmospheric missions. Bipropellant and Nuclear Thermal variants handle interplanetary flight with much higher thrust.

Each motor goes at the bottom of the rocket frame. A single motor covers a 3x3 column, but taller rockets need one motor per 3x3 column of height. The motor's thrust multiplier determines how heavy a rocket you can lift off the pad.

§ePS:§f When you upgrade to Bipropellant, the Monopropellant motor becomes your atmospheric landing thruster. It is throttleable and re-lightable, which makes it ideal for controlled descent. Most large rockets keep one for landing.
